subject: APAC onboarding: transit routes, safeguards and sign-off timeline
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@pacifichealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 04 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: APAC onboarding: transit routes, safeguards and sign-off timeline

Hi Sanjay —

Thanks for the call this morning. As discussed, we want to make sure Pacific Health's APAC region is onboarded with clear routing and data transfer safeguards before any production traffic begins. High-level asks from your side were: SCC/UK-addendum applicability, evidence for subprocessors in APAC, and a timeline we can attach to procurement.

Quick summary of Redwood's position: we support SCCs for EU exports, the UK IDTA (UK Addendum) where required, and a TIA-style mapping for regional routing (we call these TIAs/DTIAs internally). For APAC specifically, we can:
- Offer VPC/private deployment in ap-southeast-1 (customer-controlled VPC)
- Provide an onshore-traffic-only route for selected tenant endpoints (proxy edge + onshore cache)
- Produce a subprocessor evidence packet (attestations + access controls)

Action items I want to confirm today so your procurement/legal teams can schedule sign-off:
1) Which transfer mechanism do you prefer for APAC (onshore-only proxy vs. SCC + TIA mapping)?
2) Any mandatory retention/retention-scope constraints for logs (Sanjay mentioned 90 days but please confirm)?
3) If you need an HSM/KMS architecture diagram for KMS custody, we'll attach that (see attached).

I've looped in Jonas (ops) and Kimberly (legal/tech controls) to provide the attachments and a short checklist. If you can get back with a preferred mechanism by Tuesday 7/7, we can aim to have DPA redlines and evidence packet ready for procurement by 7/10.

Thanks —
Naomi Feldman
Director, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: apac-safeguards-matrix.xlsx, kms-hsm-diagram.pdf
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@pacifichealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Pacific Health Legal <legal@pacifichealth.com>, procurement@pacifichealth.com
Date: Sat, 04 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: APAC onboarding: transit routes, safeguards and sign-off timeline

Naomi —

Appreciate the follow-up. A few clarifications from procurement/legal:
- We need to confirm whether SCCs alone are sufficient for APAC traffic or if the UK IDTA/TIA mapping is expected as part of the contract. Our legal team prefers an explicit TIA mapping in the DPA when traffic crosses EU/UK boundaries, but for APAC the requirement is usually about demonstrable onshore controls and subprocessors.
- Retention: 90 days for access logs is acceptable, but any analytics-derived logs used for model tuning must be pseudonymized or kept outside customer PII scope — our privacy team will confirm language.

Can Kimberly share the exact subprocessor list and attestation cadence? Also we will need a DPA redline and a draft DocuSign we can circulate internally. Timeline-wise, procurement wants the packet by end-of-week 7/10 to meet our July onboarding window.

Thanks,
Sanjay Patel
Head of Procurement
Pacific Health

Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 05 Jul 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: APAC onboarding: transit routes, safeguards and sign-off timeline

Hi Sanjay / Legal —

Attaching the requested artifacts: apac-safeguards-matrix.xlsx (mapping of traffic lanes, TTLs, and fallback), kms-hsm-diagram.pdf (high-level KMS custody options), and a one-page attestation schedule. Summary answers below:

1) Transfer mechanism: For APAC-only processing where data never transits EU/UK, SCCs/UK IDTA are not required. If Pacific Health elects an onshore-only proxy route (we can pin endpoints to apac edge), that satisfies regional residency constraints. If you expect cross-border transfers from EU/UK into APAC, we will include a TIA/DTIA mapping and SCCs as appropriate in the DPA.

2) Subprocessors: Current APAC-affecting subprocessors are listed on page 2 of the subprocessor deck (attachment: subprocessor-deck-v2.pdf). Key ones: CloudEdge APAC (edge caches), LogStore Asia (audit logs), MetricsStream (aggregated telemetry). We produce quarterly attestations; can increase cadence to monthly for onboarding customers under procurement SLAs.

3) Retention: We can enforce a 90-day retention for access logs and 30-day for ephemeral telemetry by policy. For analytics/model tuning logs that may contain derived signals, we will provide a pseudonymization/custody statement and an export-only pathway to hold it outside of customer PII scope.

Next steps we propose:
- Pacific Health to confirm onboarding mechanism by Tue 2026-07-07 (onshore-only vs. SCC+TIA)
- Redwood legal to issue a redline DPA including TIA appendix if required; Naomi will coordinate DocuSign link
- Ops (Jonas) to provision apac-edge test endpoints upon confirmation; target readiness 7/14

Kimberly Park
Lead, Legal Ops & Data Protection
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: apac-safeguards-matrix.xlsx, kms-hsm-diagram.pdf, subprocessor-deck-v2.pdf
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@pacifichealth.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 06 Jul 2026 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: APAC onboarding: transit routes, safeguards and sign-off timeline

Sanjay / team —

Operational notes from infra:
- We can provision an ap-southeast-1 dedicated proxy and pin tenant routes to that edge. Cache TTLs and regional failover are configurable; default failover is to a non-PII degraded path to avoid cross-border PII movement.
- Subprocessor specifics: CloudEdge APAC (edge cache) will have read-only access to in-flight payloads for caching; access is logged and retained for 90 days. LogStore Asia stores audit logs encrypted at rest; we can push an HSM-backed KMS for your key custody if required.
- Performance note: Onshore-only route will add ~15-25ms median latency for global clients, but preserves residency.

I'll start provisioning a test proxy once we receive the confirmation on mechanism. Also adding a short checklist for procurement: DPA redline, KMS custody option (yes/no), required attestation cadence. For signing, here's the DocuSign draft we'll link into the ticket: https://docusign.com/documents/REDWOOD-PACIFIC-APAC-DPA-id-9981

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@pacifichealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Pacific Health Legal <legal@pacifichealth.com>, procurement@pacifichealth.com
Date: Mon, 06 Jul 2026 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: APAC onboarding: transit routes, safeguards and sign-off timeline

Thanks Naomi / Kimberly / Jonas —

This is helpful and aligned with our expectations. We will proceed with the onshore-only proxy for APAC endpoints (minimize cross-border PII). Confirming retention: 90 days for access logs, 30 days for ephemeral telemetry, analytics logs pseudonymized — legal will send specific phrasing to Kimberly.

Procurement asks that Redwood produce the redline DPA and the DocuSign by EOD 7/10 so we can review in our internal July 12 procurement committee meeting. Please mark the attestation cadence as monthly for the first three months of onboarding. We also want the KMS custody option (HSM-backed) added as an appendix so our security team can review.

Next actions for Redwood: DPA redline + DocuSign (Naomi), provide monthly attestation for first 3 months (Kimberly), and provision apac-edge test endpoint once DPA mechanism confirmed (Jonas).

I will follow up with the legal phrasing tomorrow.

Regards,
Sanjay Patel
Head of Procurement
Pacific Health
